ideas.description: Make the warmup-phase resolution stage cheaper. On the current tip (E042 commit 2b85e5e: bs 1536, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for the first 1.5 epochs then 32 px, 6.75 epochs total, SGD-group lr x1.5, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only; or I052's successor if it is kept, in which case change only its first stage), make one change: the first stage's resolution goes from 24 px to 20 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate/jitter). The stage boundary (1.5 epochs), total epochs, bs and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical. Rationale: E040 vs E043 show low-res steps are roughly free during the warmup phase but cost accuracy after it, so the cheapest lever left in that phase is to make its steps cheaper rather than more numerous. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 20 px input (expected: whitening 19, block1 19 -> pool 9, block2 9 -> pool 4, block3 4 -> pool 2, final map 2x2) and set the 20 px graph's final pool to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to that final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009 Inductor bug). In build(), warm up the 20 px train step with and without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at the 1.5-epoch switch, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Run debug_nan.py on the new graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and compare trial-0 vs later-trial train times. Eval stays the 32 px graph.
ideas.expected: Time -1.5% to -4%, point -2.8% (~5.30 s vs 5.449 s): a 20 px step has ~0.38x the block-1 FLOPs of a 32 px step vs ~0.55x at 24 px, on ~22% of steps; the fixed per-step Muon/lookahead cost is unchanged. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.15 pp, point -0.12 pp (~0.7537). Feasible means a new best. If it misses 0.753 by <=0.15 pp, keep the code path and pair it with the next accuracy gain (I053/I056). A drop >=0.4 pp means warmup-phase steps need a minimum of spatial detail; then fix the first stage at 24 px and close lower resolutions.

ideas.description: Systems change to prepare(), with the math bit-identical. At ~5.4 s per trial, prepare (0.06-0.15 s at E001) is now ~1.5-2.5% of the score and was never optimized. Gate first in drafts/ (untimed, not an experiment): call the tip's prepare() 10 times with cuda-synchronized timers around each part: reading/decoding the training files, host-to-device copy, dtype conversion/normalization, the whitening fit (patch extraction, covariance, eigendecomposition), parameter/optimizer/lookahead/RNG resets, and permutation setup. Launch only if mean prepare is >=80 ms and the math-identical cuts below save >=40 ms in drafts. Candidate cuts, all keeping results bit-identical: read the raw uint8 arrays without per-trial pickle/PIL decoding (e.g. np.load/np.fromfile/torch.frombuffer on the already-downloaded files, read only in prepare, not build); pinned host buffer plus non_blocking copy; do the uint8->half conversion and any layout change once on the GPU instead of on the CPU; remove any redundant torch.cuda.synchronize() or .item() calls; fuse per-parameter reset loops into foreach ops. Do not move anything that touches real data into build(), and do not change the whitening fit's sample set, precision or device (that would change the math). Verify in drafts/ that the final seed-0 weights of one short training are identical before and after.
ideas.expected: Time -0.5% to -2%, point -1.0% (~5.39 s). Accuracy bit-identical to the tip (deterministic per E003), so any time change is pure gain and can be kept even below the 1.5% single-run jitter bar, on the strength of the 10-repeat draft timing. If the gate shows prepare <80 ms or the cuts save <40 ms, skip the run and mark H3.1.1 as already saturated.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E042: bs 1536, the first 1.5 of 6.75 epochs at 24 px, jitter, 5.449 s at 0.7549. That leaves a 0.19 pp margin over the 0.753 gate, so pure epoch trims are off the table until an accuracy gain is banked.

**Queue after this step:** 8 queued ideas, plus I052 (the 28 px middle stage), which is running. Nothing was dropped: none of the queued ideas' hypotheses has been settled.
- **Exploit (accuracy recovery at bs 1536):** I053 head lr x2, I056 Muon lr 0.20, I059 ghost BN.
- **Exploit (time):** I057 bs 2048, plus the 2 new ideas below.
- **Explore:** I054 (NS pre-scaling, H1.9.1) and I058 (denser lookahead, H1.6.1).

**New ideas:**
1. **20 px warmup stage (H2.3, priority 3).** E040 and E043 together show that low-res steps cost almost nothing during the warmup phase, but cost accuracy after it. So the remaining lever in that phase is cheaper steps, not more of them. This keeps the 1.5-epoch boundary and replaces 24 px with 20 px. Expected: about -2.8% time and about -0.12 pp accuracy, which is borderline feasible. It pairs naturally with whichever accuracy gain lands first (I053 or I056).
2. **Math-identical prepare() trim (H3.1.1, priority 2).** Prepare is now about 2% of a 5.4 s trial and has never been optimized. It is gated by a 10-repeat timing in drafts/ and keeps accuracy bit-identical, so a gain of about 1% can be trusted even though it is below single-run jitter.

**Note for the experimenter:** I053 is written against the E040 tip. It should run on the current tip (E042, bs 1536), with the head lr doubled on top of the x1.5 SGD-group scaling. Suggested order: I053 and I056 first, to rebuild margin. Then the 20 px stage and I057 (bs 2048) can cash that margin in.
